- Overestimate prices in bullish sentiment periods (positive sentiment > 0.10) — reduce forecast by 5–10% for 30-day horizon.
- Underestimate prices after strong downward spikes (sentiment < -0.15) — add 3–5% buffer to forecast.
- Overshoots after recent price peaks — apply “mean reversion” correction: subtract 1–2% of peak value from forecast 3–5 days post-spike.
- When sentiment is consistently negative (avg < -0.10 over 5 days), reduce forecast by 2–4% for 30-day horizon.
- Forecasting 30-day ahead shows persistent lag — adjust by adding 1–3% to forecast if recent 7-day average is rising.
- If sentiment is neutral or mildly positive (0.00–0.10) and price is trending down, reduce forecast by 1–3% to avoid overconfidence bias.
